story.head: Dahlin’s favorite opponent
paras: The Lightning (11-4-2) lost 4-3 to Winnipeg on Sunday, and the Sabres (8-6-3) lost 4-1 to Vegas the same night. This is an Atlantic Division matchup, with the Bolts third (eighth in the NHL) and the Sabres sixth (tied for 17th). The Atlantic has been the strongest of the four divisions so far.

The Lightning ice the puck less than almost anyone (3rd), keep shots away from their net (3rd) and get into a lot of chippy games (4th). The Sabres rarely get pinned in their own end (4th) and get their defensemen shooting (5th), but don't block many shots (30th). The Lightning have the edge over the Sabres on the penalty kill, and something has to give when the Lightning’s shooting runs into the Sabres’ defense.

Nikita Kucherov (5 G / 17 A / 22 P in 17 GP) leads the Lightning in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Jake Guentzel (10 G / 8 A / 18 P in 17 GP) has a team-high ten goals, with seven goals in ten games against Buffalo since 2023-24. For the Sabres, Tage Thompson (10 G / 9 A / 19 P in 17 GP) leads the way in scoring, with nine points in his last five games. Jack Quinn (9 G / 7 A / 16 P in 17 GP) is next in line.

Andrei Vasilevskiy (8-4-1 / .883 SV% in 13 GS) will likely start for Tampa Bay, and Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen (5-3-3 / .878 SV% in 10 GS) for Buffalo. Vasilevskiy has a .855 save percentage in six starts against the Sabres, well under his usual .911. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.
